summary.en: Rescue operations continue after an earthquake left more than 224 dead, while protests over the removal of artworks from the National Museum have led to water-cannon use on demonstrators in Bogotá. The president is preparing to sign a decree defining maritime boundaries for the San Andres, Providencia and Santa Catalina Archipelago, and former rebel leaders have been charged with war crimes against Indigenous groups. An evangelist pastor was murdered by gang members he had evangelized, a Colombian chef was killed in a crash in Attard, and a priest died when a cross fell during a livestreamed mass. ICE agents tackled a Colombian asylum seeker in Washington, and the Mobile Anti-Riot Squad (ESMAD) has returned to operate in the country. The conflict recorded 225 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Redningsarbeidet fortsetter etter at et jordskjelv har etterlatt mer enn 224 døde, mens protester mot fjerning av kunstverk fra Nasjonalmuseet har ført til bruk av vannkanoner mot demonstranter i Bogotá. Presidenten forbereder å signere et dekret som fastsetter maritime grenser for San Andres, Providencia og Santa Catalina-øygruppen, og tidligere opprørsledere er blitt siktet for krigsforbrytelser mot urfolk. En evangelisk pastor ble drept av gjengmedlemmer han hadde evangelisert, en colombiansk kokk ble drept i en ulykke i Attard, og en prest døde da et kors falt under en direktesendt messe. ICE-agenter taklet en colombiansk asylsøker i Washington, og Mobile Anti-Riot Squad (ESMAD) er tilbake i landet. Konflikten registrerte 225 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
